name: Portrait Roma
positioning: Small all-suite residence above Via Condotti, near Piazza di Spagna, owned by the Ferragamo family's Lungarno Collection and designed by Michele Bönan around the world of Salvatore Ferragamo
best_for: Travelers who want a small, residential-style base steps from Piazza di Spagna
Fashion and design lovers drawn to the Ferragamo connection
Guests who prefer suites with living areas and kitchenettes to a full-service hotel

facts.text: Portrait Roma is set above Via Condotti, steps from Piazza di Spagna and Trinità dei Monti, overlooking the rooftops of the city.
The hotel is a short walk from the Spanish Steps and around the corner from the Six Senses and Hotel de Russie.
The hotel is owned by the Ferragamo family's Lungarno Collection, which has hotels in Florence and Milan.
Portrait Roma is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
The suites combine living areas, private terraces and discreet kitchenettes, in the style of an elegant Roman home.
The Via Condotti Suite is designed like a one-bedroom apartment.
In the Via Condotti Suite, wooden doors in the foyer hide a kitchenette with a cooking range.
Breakfast centres on Italian specialties and carefully selected ingredients.
There is no full-service restaurant; breakfast is served on the rooftop, indoors or out on the terrace.
Throughout the day the terrace is a setting for coffee, aperitivi or a glass of wine above Rome.
Guests can go shopping with a personal stylist or take a food-shopping trip to Campo de' Fiori followed by a cooking class.

highlights.text: Ferragamo memorabilia, including vintage shoe molds, hand-drawn designs and photographs of celebrity muses, line the corridors and staircases.
The hotel was designed by Michele Bönan and inspired by the world of Salvatore Ferragamo.
The Trinità dei Monti Penthouse Suite comes with a private terrace, a tiny gym and a sauna.
Portrait Roma has a rooftop terrace with panoramic views.
The concierge can procure a meal from a guest's favorite restaurant and serve it on the terrace.

considerations.text: Because it is a small, historic townhouse, fully accessible room inventory is extremely limited; check with staff when booking.
Condé Nast Traveler lists no wellness facilities at the hotel.
WhataHotel notes a limited number of rooms due to the hotel's boutique size.
